problems.title: Railworks — original Question 4
problems.source: User-uploaded Chapter9 original 'Questions' sections (verbatim, never solved)
problems.prompt: 4. Even if one accepts the court's reasoning that the contingent liability of a “mere conduit” for failure to remit transferred funds to the “initial transferee” is insufficient to make that conduit “an entity for whose benefit” an avoidable transfer was made, within the meaning of § 550(a)(1), can you nonetheless conclude that CPG had more than just this “mere conduit” contingent liability? Wasn't CPG also a guarantor of the debtor's premium debt (i.e., if the debtor had not made a premium payment to CPG, wasn't CPG personally liable to TIG for the amount of that premium payment)? If so, then why wasn't the district court correct that CPG was both a “mere conduit” and “an entity for whose benefit” the avoidable transfers at issue were made, within the meaning of § 550(a)(1)?

problems.prompt: 5. Under the court's holding, can a debtor's guarantor immunize itself from any liability as an “entity for whose benefit [a debtor's] transfer was made,” by simply requiring the debtor to make all payments on the debt through the guarantor as a “mere conduit”?
